mcp-concepts.title: MCP Fundamentals (v2)
mcp-concepts.subtitle: Master the Model Context Protocol, including the latest July 2026 v2 release

questions.text: What does MCP stand for in the context of AI assistants?
questions.hint: It's an open standard that connects AI models to external tools and data sources.

questions.text: What is the primary goal of the Model Context Protocol?
options: To standardize how AI models securely access external context (files, APIs, tools)
questions.hint: It acts like a "USB-C" port for AI applications.

questions.text: What major architectural shift was introduced in MCP v2 release - July 2026 (7.28)?
options: Transitioning to a fully stateless protocol core
questions.hint: This change allows MCP servers to easily run behind standard load balancers.

questions.text: Are MCP v2 servers backward compatible with v1 clients?
options: Yes, the specification was designed with backward compatibility in mind
Only if using the Python SDK
questions.hint: The upgrade path was designed to avoid breaking existing implementations.

questions.text: Which of the following is a new feature introduced in MCP v2?
options: Multi Round-Trip Requests for interactive tools
questions.hint: It enables tools that need back-and-forth interaction without long-lived sessions.

questions.text: What new framework was formalized in the MCP v2 release to support new protocol features?
questions.hint: It provides a standard way to extend protocol capabilities over time.

questions.text: In MCP terminology, what is a "Host"?
options: The application (like an IDE or chat interface) initiating the connection and utilizing the AI model
The external API providing the data
The physical server running the LLM
questions.hint: Claude Desktop and AI IDEs act as this component.

questions.text: Which capabilities graduated to official protocol extensions in the MCP v2 update?
questions.hint: These deal with executing background jobs and full application contexts.

questions.text: What security policy was officially introduced in the July 2026 MCP v2 release?
options: Mandatory end-to-end encryption for local processes
Authorization hardening and a formal 12-month deprecation policy
Blocking all outbound internet access by default
questions.hint: It focuses on lifecycle management and stricter auth rules.

questions.text: How does the stateless nature of MCP v2 improve production deployments?
options: It makes the protocol run faster on mobile devices
It eliminates the need for sticky sessions, simplifying horizontal scaling behind load balancers
It reduces the size of the JSON payload by 50%
It prevents the AI model from hallucinating
questions.hint: Think about how HTTP scales compared to stateful protocols.

aws-basics.title: AWS Basics
aws-basics.subtitle: Master the fundamentals of Amazon Web Services

questions.text: What is an AWS Region?
options: A physical location in the world with multiple Availability Zones
questions.hint: Think of it as a broad geographical area where AWS has data centers.

questions.text: Which AWS service is used for object storage?
questions.hint: Think "buckets" of files.

questions.text: What does EC2 stand for?
questions.hint: It's about renting virtual servers.

questions.text: Which service is a managed relational database?
questions.hint: Think MySQL, PostgreSQL, hosted by AWS.

questions.text: What is a VPC?
options: A virtual private network in AWS
questions.hint: It's your own isolated network inside AWS.

questions.text: Which AWS service delivers content via a CDN?
questions.hint: Think fast content delivery to users worldwide.

questions.text: What is the default limit on VPCs per region?
questions.hint: It's a soft limit you can request to increase.

questions.text: Which storage class is cheapest for rarely accessed data?
questions.hint: Think long-term archival storage.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling?
options: To automatically add or remove EC2 instances based on demand
To migrate on-premise databases to AWS
questions.hint: Think about maintaining application availability automatically.

questions.text: In S3, what consistency model applies to all operations as of Dec 2020?
questions.hint: AWS made a major consistency announcement for S3.

ec2-compute.title: EC2 & Compute
ec2-compute.subtitle: Learn virtual servers and compute resources

questions.text: Which IAM entity is assigned to AWS services to grant permissions securely without hardcoding credentials?
questions.hint: Used by EC2 instances or Lambda functions to assume permissions temporarily.

questions.text: What is the recommended best practice for the AWS Root Account user?
options: Use it for everyday administrative tasks
Enable MFA and lock it away, using IAM users/roles instead
Share root credentials with all team members
questions.hint: Root has unrestricted access to everything in your AWS account.

questions.text: What format are IAM policy documents written in?
questions.hint: Key-value pairs containing Version, Statement, Effect, Action, Resource.

questions.text: What does an explicit DENY in an IAM policy do when evaluated against an explicit ALLOW?
questions.hint: In AWS IAM, an explicit DENY always wins.

questions.text: Which IAM feature allows authentication via external identity providers like Google or Okta?
questions.hint: Enables Single Sign-On (SSO) with enterprise identity systems.

questions.text: What is the principle of least privilege in AWS IAM?
options: Granting only the permissions required to perform a specific task
Allowing read-only access to everyone by default
Restricting access to only the root user
questions.hint: Give users exactly what they need, and nothing more.

questions.text: What AWS service allows you to centrally manage access across multiple AWS accounts?
questions.hint: It helps you manage policies and billing across many accounts.

questions.text: Which of the following can be used to add an extra layer of security for user logins?
questions.hint: Requires a token from a device like a phone in addition to a password.

questions.text: What is a permissions boundary in IAM?
options: An advanced feature that sets the maximum permissions that an identity-based policy can grant to an IAM entity
A firewall rule that blocks IP addresses
A limit on how much money an IAM user can spend
A geographic restriction on where an IAM user can log in
questions.hint: It acts as an upper limit on permissions, even if a policy allows more.

questions.text: When evaluating an IAM policy, what happens if there is no explicit ALLOW or explicit DENY for an action?
options: The action is allowed if the user is in the admin group
questions.hint: AWS defaults to "no" unless specifically told "yes".

azure-devops.title: Azure DevOps Fundamentals
azure-devops.subtitle: Learn Azure Boards, Pipelines, Repos, and Artifacts

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of Azure Pipelines?
questions.hint: It automates the building, testing, and deployment of your code.

questions.text: Which Azure DevOps service is used for agile project management and work tracking?
questions.hint: Think Kanban boards, sprints, and backlogs.

questions.text: What type of version control systems does Azure Repos support?
questions.hint: It supports both distributed and centralized Microsoft version control.

questions.text: What format is primarily used to define Azure Pipelines as code?
questions.hint: It's the most common human-readable data serialization language used for CI/CD configurations.

questions.text: What is an Azure DevOps "Agent"?
options: Computing infrastructure that runs your pipeline jobs
questions.hint: It's the machine (Microsoft-hosted or self-hosted) that executes your build scripts.

questions.text: Which service in Azure DevOps allows you to create, host, and share packages like npm, NuGet, and Maven?
questions.hint: Think of it as a private package manager repository.

questions.text: What is a Pipeline "Stage" in Azure Pipelines?
options: A logical boundary in the pipeline (e.g., Build, Test, Deploy to Prod)
questions.hint: It's used to organize pipeline execution into phases, often requiring approvals to move between them.

questions.text: What feature allows you to pause a pipeline execution until a human reviews and allows it to proceed?
questions.hint: Typically configured on an Environment before deploying to Production.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a native Work Item type in the default Agile process in Azure Boards?
questions.hint: The first three represent work, whereas the fourth is a timebox (iteration).

questions.text: How does Azure DevOps handle secrets and sensitive configuration values in Pipelines?
options: Storing them in plain text in YAML
Using Pipeline Variable Groups linked to Azure Key Vault
questions.hint: It integrates with Azure's native cryptographic storage service.

gcp-fundamentals.subtitle: Learn Google Cloud infrastructure, Compute Engine, and BigQuery

questions.text: What is the primary IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) offering in Google Cloud Platform?
questions.hint: It provides scalable virtual machines.

questions.text: Which GCP service is designed for serverless, fully managed container execution?
questions.hint: It runs stateless containers on a fully managed environment.

questions.text: What is Google Cloud's fully managed, serverless data warehouse?
questions.hint: It allows super-fast SQL queries on massive datasets.

questions.text: How does GCP organize resources hierarchically?
questions.hint: Projects sit below folders and above individual resources.

questions.text: Which database service provides horizontal scaling, strong consistency, and relational semantics globally?
questions.hint: It's the only enterprise-grade, globally-distributed, and strongly consistent database service built for the cloud.

questions.text: What is the default global load balancing service for HTTP(S) traffic in GCP?
questions.hint: It distributes web traffic across multiple regions automatically.

questions.text: What is the difference between standard and nearline storage classes in Cloud Storage?
options: Standard is for archival, nearline is for frequent access
Standard is for frequent access, nearline is for data accessed less than once a month
Standard is multi-regional only, nearline is regional only
questions.hint: Nearline is slightly cheaper for storage but incurs retrieval costs.

questions.text: Which of the following is true about VPC networks in GCP compared to AWS?
options: GCP VPCs are regional, AWS VPCs are global
GCP VPCs are global resources, AWS VPCs are regional
questions.hint: In GCP, a single VPC can span multiple regions without peering.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of Google Cloud Identity and Access Management (IAM) service accounts?
options: To allow external users to log in
To provide an identity for an application or VM to interact with other GCP services
questions.hint: It's an identity that belongs to your application or virtual machine, not an individual end user.

questions.text: Which GCP service provides a fully managed, Apache Kafka-compatible messaging service?
questions.hint: It's an asynchronous messaging service designed for streaming analytics and data integration pipelines.
